cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Ewe Keta cloth: a strip-woven cotton wrapper with warp-striped and weft-float block patterns in the colors and layout typical of southern Ghana/Togo Ewe weaving. It clearly matches a garment/textile made and worn by the Ewe.

physical.title: textile; wrapper
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 18 strips of hand-woven cotton, hand-sewn together along the selvages. All the cotton is industrial European thread of five colours: white, blue, red, green and yellow. There are two different warp patterns, which are arranged alternately across the cloth. The first pattern is warp-faced, and consists of  symmetrically arranged stripes of dark blue, white, red and yellow; the weft is of dark blue. The second pattern has a white warp through which run 12 narrow and two broad line of the dark blue. Its weft is of white cotton, interspersed at regular intervals by triple narrow stripes of blue; the main design is created by weaving two or three weft blocks per strip using a second pair of heddles; these are in a variety of sequences of line of red, black, green, blue and white. The warp ends have hand-sewn hems.
